title: Sieve Season
mech: A 4-notch gauge bar stretches a printed auxetic lattice deck so all 35 cells widen at once, and each notch releases exactly one grade of seed into the chutes below.
blurb: Four players sow graded seed onto one shared flexible sieve; pulling the gauge bar opens every cell at once and drops a whole grade into the scoring chutes.
idea: The board is a single printed re-entrant honeycomb (auxetic) lattice with negative Poisson's ratio: pulling its free edge lengthwise makes every one of its 35 cells grow wider in both directions at the same time. A detented gauge bar sets that stretch in four steps, and the seed pieces are truncated cones in three collar diameters, sized so each notch releases exactly one grade. That single shared variable drives the whole decision loop: on your turn you either sow a seed into the lowest empty cell of a column, or crank the bar one notch, which simultaneously harvests every released seed on the deck into the seven chutes below and deletes that grade from everyone's legal plays for the rest of the season. Scoring is area majority per chute with a hard physical capacity of five seeds, so cranking is at once a harvest, a denial, and a clock. There is no hidden information and no randomizer; the tension is purely about when the bar moves.
identity: like Connect Four + a printed auxetic (negative-Poisson) sieve lattice whose one gauge bar widens all 35 cells at once, so each notch drops one whole grade of piece out of the board and into the scoring chutes
